title: Redwood POC scoping with EdgeCare - security pilot
next_steps: Send SOC 2 / ISO pack and security questionnaire
Share benchmark spreadsheet and expected workload template
Schedule SE deep dive for network/VPC setup (Marcus + Mark)
Draft SOW for 4-week pilot and share pricing options
action_items: Lena: send SOC2 report + security questionnaire by 2027-11-04
Marcus: share benchmark scripts and runner config by 2027-11-05
Priya: provide sample traffic profile (concurrency and tokens) by 2027-11-07
Mark: confirm allowed IPs / VPN access and SSO metadata by 2027-11-06
summary: POC scoping focused on security/compliance requirements for a 4-week pilot. Discussed SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, and on-prem/VPC options. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share benchmark templates, schedule technical deep dive, finalize pilot SOW.
transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for making time, this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the deal. We have Marcus from the SE team as well. Quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: Priya Patel, CIO at EdgeCare, thanks.
[00:12] Mark: Mark Dawson, InfoSec.
[00:14] Sofia: Sofia Ruiz, head of AI/ML.
[00:17] Tom: Tom Bennett, compliance.
[00:19] Lena: Great, today's agenda is to scope the POC, confirm success criteria, sizing and most importantly your security and compliance requirements for the pilot. Marcus will cover benchmarks and network setup.
[00:30] Marcus: Hi all, yeah I'll go over the technical plan, we're aiming for a 4-week pilot, can be 2-6 weeks depending on scope. We'll run baseline benchmarks and then a representative workload.
[00:40] Priya: High level goal — we want to evaluate production viability for a patient-facing summarization service, latency under 800ms median, throughput for about 120 concurrent sessions, and ensure there are no data leakage risks. Security is non-negotiable.
[00:54] Mark: Right, and from InfoSec side we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO 27001 cert copy if you have it, and the answers to our security questionnaire — encryption at rest, in transit, KMS/HSM, key rotation policies, and separation of customer data.
[01:10] Lena: We have SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 scope. I'll attach the artifacts. On encryption, Redwood supports TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest via KMS. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
[01:25] Tom: How do you handle audit logs and access logging? We need immutable logs for user access and admin actions retained for at least 1 year and exports for audits.
[01:36] Marcus: Audit logs are available in the Console — token-level traces, admin actions, model route changes; we can export logs to your S3 or to the SIEM over secure delivery. Retention windows are configurable for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can discuss extended retention as an add-on.
[01:50] Sofia: For the pilot we need RBAC such that only certain users can invoke models for production endpoints; data scientists should have eval access but not production key. Do you support fine-grained RBAC and SSO?
[02:02] Lena: Yes, SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning is supported. RBAC roles are configurable — admin, dev, observer, eval, etc. We'll share the role matrix.
[02:12] Mark: SSO is key. Also we need to know if you support federated auth with our IdP and whether the metadata can be exchanged before the pilot start.
[02:20] Marcus: Yes, we can accept SAML metadata. For Private or Dedicated deployments we can also establish a VPC peering or VPN for network isolation.
[02:30] Priya: Data residency — some PHI may be touched in logs, so need to confirm data at rest in region X, and that Redwood will not use the data to improve models.
[02:40] Lena: We have a data usage policy for dedicated and private customers: no customer data is used for model training. For hosted accounts we have options to opt-out, but the guaranteed no-use policy is for Dedicated/Private. We'll provide the clause for the SOW.
[02:54] Tom: We also need to be sure about redaction and PII handling in telemetry. Can telemetry be sanitized before leaving customer network?
[03:02] Marcus: For Private we can keep logs in your network; for Dedicated we can configure prefix caching and redaction rules and filter PII with transform hooks. I'll detail available options in the follow-up doc.
[03:15] Sofia: On the benchmark side — our expected workload is primarily short prompts with some 2–3k token contexts for chart summarization. Typical request size is 800 tokens resp avg, with spikes up to 3k.
[03:28] Marcus: Good — for sizing we need avg tokens per request, peak RPS, concurrency and target latency SLO. You mentioned 120 concurrent; what's your peak RPS?
[03:36] Priya: Peak around 40 rps, sustained 20 rps, with burstability during morning rounds.
[03:44] Marcus: OK that maps to roughly X GPU footprint — we'll propose an instance mix. For the pilot we can run on hosted with a dedicated capacity pool so you get isolation without full private deployment. This accelerates start.
[03:56] Mark: We need to confirm network controls — IP allowlist, private endpoints, and the ability to disable public access. Can Redwood provide a private endpoint in our VPC?
[04:05] Marcus: We offer Private deployment (VPC) and Dedicated with private endpoints. For the pilot we can do a dedicated pool with an allowlist and VPC peering. We'll document options and friction points.
[04:16] Tom: What about logging of admin keys and rotation? We have strict key rotation policies and need HSM-backed keys.
[04:24] Lena: We support KMS integration and HSM in Private deployments. For Dedicated we can integrate with a customer-managed KMS or provide our managed keys with rotation policies.
[04:34] Sofia: For acceptance criteria for the POC — from product: latency median <800ms for 90% requests, functional correctness on summarization tests, no major security exceptions from your InfoSec runbook, and integration with SSO + RBAC.
[04:47] Priya: Also need data handling signoff from compliance and proof points for audit logging and retention.
[04:53] Marcus: Proposed pilot plan: Week 0 (prep): exchange security docs, SAML metadata, whitelist IPs, share sample traffic. Week 1: baseline benchmarks and connectivity. Week 2–3: run representative workload and measure latency/cost. Week 4: results review, security sign-off and decision.
[05:10] Mark: For the security questionnaire, expect to see details on penetration testing cadence, vulnerability disclosure, patching windows and SLA on incident response.
[05:20] Lena: Yes we'll include pentest reports and our incident response playbook.
[05:24] Tom: Any data access restrictions for Redwood engineers during the pilot? We need to control who can see logs.
[05:31] Marcus: Access controls can be restricted with RBAC and we can provide jumpbox access through your bastion for troubleshooting; engineer access is logged and can be made read-only unless escalated.
[05:42] Sofia: Benchmarks — can you run both raw latency and p99 tail? We need p50, p95, p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:50] Marcus: Yes. We'll deliver a bench spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, tokens per sec, cost-per-token estimate for quantized model options. We'll also run a synthetic suite and replay with a subset of redacted production traces if you can supply them.
[06:05] Priya: About redaction — we can supply sanitized traces. That should be fine.
[06:08] Lena: On pricing — pilot pricing is usually credits-based for hosted/dedicated, and we can propose a pilot rate plus a conversion path to committed Dedicated capacity if you proceed. I'll include options in the SOW.
[06:21] Mark: A few technical questions: do you support bringing-your-own-models? If we want to run a fine-tuned model inside the pilot, what are constraints?
[06:30] Marcus: We support model onboarding. For private/dedicated we can host your model artifacts. For hosted we have a model catalog and model variant options; bringing your own may require extra review and signing for IP handling.
[06:42] Tom: Compliance wants to see who has access to model artifacts and where they're stored.
[06:47] Marcus: We'll document storage locations and access controls.
[06:51] Sofia: Some of our usage will hit KV cache and long-context inference. Any limits we should know about for cache sizes and eviction?
[06:58] Marcus: We have configurable KV cache sizes and policies. For long-context models we recommend specific kernel paths and quantization settings; we'll advise in the tuning doc.
[07:09] Priya: Is there any risk of Redwood using our customer prompts for model improvement? You said no for Dedicated/Private, but clarify for hosted.
[07:18] Lena: Hosted customers have an opt-out clause for data usage; however default may be different per plan. We'll include explicit language: for the pilot we recommend Dedicated pool with the contractual no-use clause.
[07:30] Mark: Where are your logs stored geographically? We need EU-only storage for some of our tenants.
[07:36] Marcus: Region placement is configurable — we can pin storage and compute to specific cloud regions. We'll call that out in the pilot config.
[07:44] Tom: Can you provide a sample SIEM integration — e.g., Splunk or Datadog mapping?
[07:50] Marcus: Yes, we have documented log schemas and sample integrations — we'll attach examples to the follow-up.
[07:58] Priya: For the pilot success criteria, can we have a short written sign-off checklist?
[08:03] Lena: Absolutely. Draft acceptance checklist: connectivity verified, SSO + RBAC in place, latency SLOs met on representative workload, audit logs captured and exported, security questionnaire signed, and cost estimates provided.
[08:20] Sofia: On timelines — can we start next week? We need the SAML metadata and sample traces ASAP.
[08:25] Lena: We'll target kickoff on Monday 2027-11-08 if we get artifacts by 2027-11-06. Marcus will need network person and Mark to confirm access.
[08:33] Marcus: I'll book a deep dive for network/VPC on 2027-11-05 — Mark please invite your infra person.
[08:39] Mark: Will do.
[08:41] Tom: A couple of oddities we've seen with transcripts — sorry — on logging, do you have an immutable write-once log for audit?
[08:48] Marcus: We can deliver immutable audit streams to your S3 and enable object lock. For console logs we have append-only event streams in Dedicated/Private modes.
[08:58] Priya: Ok good. Another question: how quickly can you rotate to a Private deployment if the pilot goes well?
[09:06] Lena: Typical lead time is 4–8 weeks depending on contract and infra. We can run pilot on Dedicated capacity and then convert to Private with additional work. We'll outline migration options.
[09:18] Sofia: Cost visibility during pilot — we need per-route token cost and estimates for scaling to peak.
[09:24] Marcus: Console provides token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards. We'll share a sample export and the cost model assumptions.
[09:33] Priya: Any regulatory support for HIPAA? We may need a BAA.
[09:38] Lena: We can sign BAAs for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted may be evaluated case-by-case. We'll bring legal ops into the thread.
[09:47] Mark: For the security questionnaire: items around vulnerability management — do you publish CVE handling and patch SLA?
[09:54] Marcus: We publish our vulnerability disclosure policy, and typically respond within 30 days for critical fixes; we'll include specifics.
[10:04] Tom: One last thing — we want RBAC to prevent data scientists from exporting logs out of the system. Can you sandbox export permissions?
[10:12] Marcus: Yes exports are permissioned, and we can limit S3 write roles to specific service accounts.
[10:18] Lena: OK wrapping up. Recap: deliver SOC2 and ISO docs, security questionnaire answers, benchmark templates, schedule network deep dive, draft SOW for 4-week pilot, and sample SSO metadata exchange.
[10:30] Priya: Good recap. We'll aim to get sample traces and SAML metadata by 11/06.
[10:35] Mark: I'll get the infra contact and IP allowlist.
[10:38] Sofia: We're excited to test the summarization flow.
[10:41] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[10:43] Lena: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[10:47] Marcus: Thanks.
[10:50] END TRANSCRIPT
